approach: Add crates/athena-core/src/preflight.rs. It lists the programs a capability's checks run, looks each bare name up in the absolute PATH entries through an injectable `ToolProbe` (the system probe scans PATH and runs nothing), and returns every program considered plus blockers, each with a non-empty workaround. Path programs and tools that only a relative PATH entry could supply are listed as "not probed", never dropped. `Athena::dispatch` (run/mod.rs) calls it right after `capability.checks(&jc)`, writes one redacted line per program into the existing `Job.note` (committed in the prediction commit before any agent runs), and on a blocker closes the job `failed` with an `environment: preflight blocked: ...` reason through a new `stop_preflight` in run/pin.rs. That is possible because pin.rs is a child module of `run` and sees the private `Closing`, `RunContext` and `failure`, as planning.rs does for `stop_planning`. A blocked retry leaves the earlier job's kept work alone. The retry link is fixed where it is made: `Athena::retry` (reading.rs) retries the job a preflight-stopped job had retried, so the stored request of the next job reads `try again on <J1>` and every reader of that link (dispatch seeds, reader context, gate counts, evidence labels, steward, status, scope guard) sees the real chain. The spec entry and one CHANGELOG line follow. A missing bare-name check program used to land with a recorded pre-existing failure (checks.rs:541-562; lifecycle.rs:150-152). It now stops the job as an environment blocker. The plan says so everywhere and limits the 0% estimate to this repository's checks.

decisions.choice: Needed programs are the first element of each check's `run`, each listed once with the names of its checks. A bare name (non-empty, no `/`) is probed. A name containing `/` is not probed and is recorded as `<last path component>: not probed (path)`. Git, gh and the agent binary are not needs of their own.
decisions.reason: Today a check program that cannot start is not a failure of the job: checks.rs:541-562 turns the spawn error into a failed CheckRun ('could not start'), and lifecycle.rs:128-152 asserts the job still lands because the same failure is pre-existing on the base. The preflight is therefore a deliberate behavior change for bare-name programs. A path program resolves against the check's working directory (a relative path may name a file the producer creates) or an absolute place Athena does not control, so it cannot be judged a missing capability in advance; it is listed with the reason. Git: Athena runs git before the hook (`JobConfig::at` run/mod.rs:1029, `pin_repo` 1100, the prediction commit 1261), so a git blocker could never be recorded; a check that runs `git` is still probed as a check program. gh never changes a job's outcome (gh/early.rs:425-437 only warns) and landing is a later command. The agent binary is already checked: `ClaudeCodeDriver::new` (athena-agent/src/claude.rs:89) calls `check_pinned` (claude.rs:49-63), which runs `<bin> --version` and compares the pinned version, so a missing binary fails before any job is dispatched. The preflight does not repeat that, and the code comment and spec mechanism say so (finding 3).

rejected.why: A relative path may name a file the producer creates; the rewrite would stop testing the 'could not start' baseline path and edit a test file outside the deliverables.

decisions.choice: `ToolProbe::probe(&self, tool: &str) -> Probe` with `Probe::{Present, Missing, NotProbed(&'static str)}`. `SystemProbe { path: Option<OsString> }` (`from_env()`, `with_path(..)` for tests) splits PATH with `std::env::split_paths`. Only absolute entries are searched; a candidate counts when `std::fs::metadata` says it is a file with any execute bit (unix). If no absolute entry has the tool but PATH holds a relative or empty entry, the answer is `NotProbed("relative PATH")`, not Missing. Nothing is run. Three limits are written in the doc comment and the spec mechanism: it reads Athena's own PATH; relative entries are not judged; 'any execute bit' is looser than the kernel's check.
decisions.reason: Finding 4: checks spawn with `.current_dir(ctx.dir)` (checks.rs:532-536), so a relative PATH entry such as `node_modules/.bin` resolves against the job directory, not Athena's working directory; searching it from Athena's cwd could wrongly block or wrongly pass. Finding 3 of the earlier round still holds: checks run with `env_clear().envs(ctx.env)` (checks.rs:534-535), built from `env_pass` plus capability `env` templates (athena-agent/src/env.rs:70-74, 101-109); this repository passes PATH (athena.toml:52) and sets no PATH template, so the probe and the checks agree here. A PATH scan is what `Command::new` does and has no side effects. Running `<tool> --version` (the accepted reading's wording) would run whatever script athena.toml names, can hang, and a kill leaves grandchildren; the aim, a probe a test can inject, is kept.

Dispatch tests use the real probe: bare name `athena-preflight-absent-tool` (on no PATH) for missing, `true` for present.

decisions.choice: Record in the existing `Job.note` (Option<String>, athena-data/src/records.rs:625), set at the Job literal (run/mod.rs:1250, now `None`; the `note: None` at 1227 belongs to `Owner`), committed in the prediction commit (1261) before any agent runs. One line per program: `<tool>: present`, `<tool>: missing`, `<last component>: not probed (path)` or `<tool>: not probed (relative PATH)`, each followed by `needed by <checks>`; with no check programs the note is `no check programs to probe`. Path programs are recorded by last component only, and the whole note goes through `redactor.redact(..)?` (the `redactor` at run/mod.rs:1096) before it is set. The blocker and workaround are also in the closing reason.
decisions.reason: Finding 5: an absolute path from athena.toml could carry a home directory into job.json on the records branch; last component plus the redactor closes that. A job stopped before the producer has no candidate or plan, so a Blocker Finding in a Verification or Critique record has nowhere to live (records.rs:896-913, plan.rs:159-173); the brief allows no new record or data file. Nothing reads or prints `Job.note` (status.rs and display.rs do not): the per-tool record is visible only in job.json, and the stop reason is the only part a command shows, only for a blocked job. The spec mechanism says this.

decisions.choice: Stop reason `environment: preflight blocked: <tool> (needed by <checks>) is not on PATH; workaround: <steps>`, plus `; the kept work of <earlier> was left alone; a retry of this job resumes it` when an earlier job's work was left alone. New `pub(super) fn stop_preflight(&self, ctx: &RunContext<'_>, closing: &mut Closing, reason: &str)` in run/pin.rs sets `closing.happened = self.failure(ctx, reason)` and `verification_passed = None`, like `stop_planning` (planning.rs:8-14). Dispatch then returns `self.close_dispatched(&ctx, closing)`.
decisions.reason: This corrects the earlier plan, which wrongly said pin.rs could not name `Closing`/`RunContext`: they are private items of module `run` (mod.rs:121, 1369, `failure` at 2470), and pin.rs is its child module (`mod pin;` mod.rs:65, `use super::*` pin.rs:3), the same way planning.rs reaches them. pin.rs is a listed deliverable and now has a real change. `StopCause::of` (disk.rs:450-463) classifies any `environment:` reason as `OtherEnvironment` with no change to disk.rs, and the scope guard does not count it as a failure of the work (scope_guard.rs:565-568).

rejected.why: Counts as a failure of the work and could raise the retry signal.

decisions.choice: A blocked job keeps an earlier job's work. `dispatch` computes `earlier` (the job of `retry_seed`, `resume`, `resume_from` or `stale_conflict`) once the seeds are known; on a blocker the RunContext is built with `resume: None`, so `close_dispatched` does not call `remove_kept_work` (run/close.rs:152-154) and `settle_resume_marks` (run/mod.rs:860-874) leaves the mark alone.
decisions.reason: A stop that did none of the work must not destroy the earlier job's kept work.

decisions.choice: Fix the retry link where it is made, in `Athena::retry` (reading.rs:1185-1234). New pure `preflight::retry_target(records: &Records, id: &JobId) -> JobId`: while the job is closed `failed` with a reason for which `is_preflight_reason` holds and its own request names another job through `retried_job`, move to that job (at most 16 hops, stops on a cycle or an unknown job); otherwise return `id`. `retry` uses the target for `request = format!("{RETRY_PREFIX}{target}")`, for `has_retry_introspection` (1212), for `resumable_job` and for `read_resume` (1221-1222), and prints one line saying job `<id>` stopped at the capability preflight without doing work and the retry is of `<target>`. The pause check (1191) and the interrupted-retry guard (1199-1211) keep using the id the user gave. `dispatch` needs no special follow; the `through_preflight_stops` of the earlier plan is dropped.
decisions.reason: Finding 2. The stored request text is the link every reader reads through `retried_job`: gate_counts.rs:119 (a gate that ended J1 counts as overruled when a landed job's request retries J1), evidence_labels.rs:173 (`retry_vote`), steward.rs:454, status/throughput.rs:604, status/planning.rs:325, scope_guard.rs:667 and reading/retry.rs:229 (`job_history`). With J3 stored as `try again on J1`, all of them see J1→J3 with no change, and the dispatch seeds (`tree_seed`, `timeout_seed` 888, `resume_seed`, `stale_seed` 579, `retry_findings`, `planning_resume_seed` 530) and `earlier_attempt_with` (retry.rs:22-82, which already carries the original request of a chain) read J1 directly. Every caller of `Athena::retry` gets it, including the drain (drain.rs:4610 `ReadOf::Retry`) and `athena retry` (athena-cli/src/commands.rs:27). For a job that is not a preflight stop `retry_target` returns `id`, so every other retry is unchanged. J2 stays on the record as a failed attempt of J1's line (scope_guard.rs:667, an environment verdict as before). J2 is a sibling of J3 under J1, which is accurate: J2 did no work.

A study has no check programs unless configured, so the pin cost applies only to the rare combination. The check list is only known at 1153 for the same reason as the brief's check views (1155-1161).

steps: Create crates/athena-core/src/preflight.rs. `needed_tools(&[CheckSpec])` returns one `Need` per `run[0]` (empty `run` skipped), each program once with the names of the checks that need it; a bare name (non-empty, no `/`) is probed, a name with `/` is kept as not probed (path) and displayed by its last component; git, gh and the agent binary are never added on their own (comment cites claude.rs:49-63, 89 for the agent binary and run/mod.rs:1029, 1100, 1261 for git). `SystemProbe::probe` searches absolute PATH entries only, using `std::fs::metadata` for a file with any execute bit, and answers `NotProbed("relative PATH")` when the tool is absent but PATH holds a relative or empty entry; it runs nothing. A follow-up outside these deliverables is to make a preflight stop end the drain like LowDisk.

demonstrations.method: Tests in run/tests.rs go through `Athena::go` into `dispatch` (run/mod.rs:402, 1015) and `Athena::retry` (reading.rs:1185) with the existing harness (`repo()`, `athena_with(&repo,&state,check,plenty_of_space,script)`, `finished_job`, `counting`, `producer_ending`, Docs capability). TEST A `capability_preflight_blocks_a_missing_tool_before_the_producer_and_records_it`: check `&["athena-preflight-absent-tool"]`, script `counting(counts, None)`; asserts Failed, a reason starting `environment: preflight blocked:` naming the tool and `workaround`, `is_environment_reason`, `StopCause::of == OtherEnvironment`, zero producer and verifier calls, and, loading `Records` at `finished.prediction_commit`, a Job `note` containing `athena-preflight-absent-tool: missing`, no candidate yet. TEST B `capability_preflight_records_every_probed_tool_when_all_are_present`: check `PASSES` (`true`); asserts the producer ran once, the reason does not start with `environment:`, and the Job record at `finished.prediction_commit` (before any candidate, showing the order) has a note containing `true: present`; a variant with a second check named by an absolute path under a fake home directory shows its `not probed (path)` line with only the last component and no directory. TEST C `capability_preflight_stop_on_a_resumed_retry_keeps_the_earlier_work`: a first Athena with `producer_ending(Error, &expired_login(), true, ..)` closes failed with a login-expiry stop and keeps a candidate commit but no kept directory (tests.rs:5368-5369), so after `finished_job` the test creates `athena.state.kept_work_dir(&first)` by hand with `create_dir_all` (as tests.rs:5249-5250). A second Athena over the same repo and state tempdirs (`athena_with`) has check `athena-preflight-absent-tool`; `retry(first)` then `go`. Asserts: Failed with the preflight reason naming `first`; `kept_work_dir(&first)` still exists; the first job's candidate commit is still in the repository. TEST D `capability_preflight_retry_of_a_stopped_job_resumes_the_job_it_retried`: a third Athena with check `PASSES` runs `retry(stopped)`; asserts the returned proposal's stored request text is `try again on <first>` and `retried_job(&records, text) == Some(first)` (the one function gate_counts, evidence_labels, steward, throughput, status/planning and scope_guard read the link through); then `go` finishes, the producer ran once, the dispatch commit's producer brief names `first` as the job retried and carries the first job's progress note, and `kept_work_dir(&first)` is gone. TEST E `capability_preflight_retry_of_a_plain_stop_is_unchanged`: a job that failed for another reason, and a preflight-stopped job whose own request is not a retry, both get `try again on <that job>` as before.

demonstrations.observes: A: Failed with the environment reason, no producer call, blocker in the note and the outcome.
